A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GUAVA and contain readable methods, equations, experiments, figures, tables, and appendices. Retained and relocated material can be matched reliably across versions.

before.justification: V1 reports original self-reenactment and cross-reenactment experiments, baseline comparisons, and component ablations in Tables 1–4, alongside qualitative reconstruction and tracking results.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds qualitative extreme-view, full-body, and failure-case results in Appendix C.

M1.justification: EHM tracking, the template and UV Gaussian branches, inverse texture mapping, the refiner, and training losses remain unchanged, including Appendix B. The full-body demonstration does not document a modified algorithm; preprocessing labels clarify the existing procedure.

E1.justification: V2 adds full-body reconstruction and animation, plus extreme-angle and back-facing novel-view examples in Appendix C.1–C.2 and Figures 9–10. These extend the demonstrated scenarios beyond v1's upper-body evaluations, while the original training sources and benchmark datasets remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain MimicMotion, Champ, and MagicPose as 2D baselines, and ExAvatar, GaussianAvatar, and GART as 3D baselines. Newly cited works such as IDOL are discussed but are not added as evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 revises reported training compute from approximately 78 to 156 GPU hours, while retaining 200,000 iterations and batch size 12. This changes the reported resource setting without establishing that experiments were rerun. Existing splits, metrics, and baseline evaluation procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds extreme-view extrapolation examples and failure-case visualizations for fluffy hair, loose clothing, and flowing folds in Figures 9 and 11. These provide concrete evidence for weaknesses already discussed in v1. Existing component ablations and EHM tracking comparisons are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, experimental seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Both retain point-estimate tables, and the added qualitative examples introduce no uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 retain their numerical values and rankings, including GUAVA's 25.87 PSNR and 52.21 FPS in Table 1 and 0.5554 IPS in Table 3. V2 adds qualitative full-body, extreme-view, and failure outputs in Figures 9–11, including degraded back-facing rendering.

T1.justification: Equations 1–8, including deformation, reconstruction losses, and tracking objectives, are retained. Identifying k as the triangle index explains a symbol already present in the Gaussian representation; it introduces no substantive mathematical definition, assumption, or derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: generalizable single-image upper-body Gaussian reconstruction, enhanced facial expressiveness through EHM, improved rendering, and real-time animation. The additional appendix demonstrations do not redefine these core contributions.

C2.justification: Figure 1 and Section 4.2 explicitly qualify the reconstruction-speed statement as starting from a tracked image. Appendix C adds a full-body applicability qualification tied to scarce full-body training data and discusses back-view degradation. Hair, clothing, and frontal-view limitations were already acknowledged in v1.

D1.justification: Reported training time changes from 78 to 156 GPU hours in Section 4.1. V2 clarifies tracking as preprocessing and explains the triangle-index parameter k. Appendix hyperparameters, feature dimensions, tracking iterations, and project-access information otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds five cited works, including IDOL, HRAvatar, and SLGaussian, and removes DreamGaussian and 3D Gaussian Blendshapes for Head Avatar Animation. Most changes update existing citation lists; Appendix C.1 additionally presents IDOL's use of 360-degree training data as a possible direction for improving back views.

P1.justification: Edits refine selected captions, parameter explanations, and efficiency prose. Appendix C gains full-body and failure-case subsections, while Appendix D becomes a discussion section containing EHM-versus-SMPLX commentary and the retained ethics text. The main narrative and section organization remain largely intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds Figures 9–11, relocates the retained novel-view figure, and moves and renumbers the original EHM tracking Figure 9 as Figure 12. Figure 2 gains preprocessing labels and minor graphical adjustments. Existing benchmark tables and other main experimental figures retain their presentation.

improvement.justification: V2 clarifies that the advertised reconstruction time starts from a tracked image and adds visual evidence of extreme-view, hair, and clothing limitations previously described mainly in prose. These changes improve transparency and help readers assess applicability. The gains are limited because the central method and quantitative benchmark evidence remain unchanged, and the new scenarios receive qualitative demonstrations.
